claims.object_text: ancient transcription factor orchestrating neurodevelopmental processes in the rostral brain
claims.quote: Foxg1 is an ancient transcription factor gene orchestrating a number of neurodevelopmental processes taking place in the rostral brain.
mice overexpressing Foxg1 in neocortical pyramidal cells displayed an electroencephalography (EEG) with increased spike frequency

claims.object_text: increased susceptibility to kainic acid-induced seizures
claims.quote: were more prone to kainic acid (KA)-induced seizures.

claims.object_text: hyperactivity and hypersynchronization of primary neocortical neuron cultures
claims.quote: primary cultures of neocortical neurons gain-of-function for Foxg1 were hyperactive and hypersynchronized.

claims.object_text: unbalanced expression of genes encoding ion channels, GABA and glutamate receptors
claims.quote: an unbalanced expression of key genes encoding for ion channels, gamma aminobutyric acid and glutamate receptors
was likely exacerbated by a pronounced interneuron depletion.

claims.object_text: transient activity-dependent upregulation mediated by immediate early genes
claims.quote: a transient Foxg1 upregulation ignited in turn by neuronal activity and mediated by immediate early genes.

claims.object_text: small changes in Foxg1 levels can profoundly impact pyramidal cell activity
claims.quote: even small changes of Foxg1 levels may result in a profound impact on pyramidal cell activity
